# Equations and tables {short-title="Equations and tables"}

This chapter covers mathematical syntax (inline equations, numbered block equations,
advanced environments) and two levels of tables: simple Markdown pipe tables and
enriched tables via the `quartable` extension.

## Inline equations {#sec-eq-inline}

Inline equations are written between dollar signs: `$...$`. In PDF they use the native
LaTeX math mode; in HTML they are rendered by KaTeX.

````markdown
The Fourier transform of a function $f$ is defined by
$\hat{f}(\xi) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,\mathrm{d}x$.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

The Fourier transform of a function $f$ is defined by
$\hat{f}(\xi) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,\mathrm{d}x$.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Thin spaces in mathematics

Use `\,` for thin spaces: `f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x` gives $f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$.
Use `\mathrm{d}` (roman) rather than `d` (italic) for differentials — this is the
ISO 80000-2 standard.
:::

## Numbered block equations {#sec-eq-block}

Block equations are delimited by `$$...$$`. To number them and create a cross-reference,
add `{#eq-label}`:

````markdown
$$
i\hbar\frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial t} = \hat{H}\Psi
$$ {#eq-schrodinger}

The Schrödinger equation (@eq-schrodinger) describes the time evolution…
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

$$
i\hbar\frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial t} = \hat{H}\Psi
$$ {#eq-schrodinger}

:::

The Schrödinger equation (@eq-schrodinger) describes the time evolution of a quantum
system.

::: {.callout-warning}
## `@eq-label` without brackets

An equation cross-reference is written `@eq-label`, **without brackets**. Brackets
`[@eq-label]` are reserved for bibliographic citations and will not work for equations.
:::

## Advanced mathematical environments {#sec-eq-advanced}

LaTeX environments such as `aligned`, `cases`, `bmatrix` work natively in Quarto,
both in PDF (pure LaTeX) and in HTML (KaTeX):

````markdown
$$
\begin{cases}
  \dot{x}(t) = Ax(t) + Bu(t) \\
  y(t) = Cx(t) + Du(t)
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-statespace}
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

$$
\begin{cases}
  \dot{x}(t) = Ax(t) + Bu(t) \\
  y(t) = Cx(t) + Du(t)
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-statespace}

:::

The state-space representation (@eq-statespace) is the standard form in control theory.

````markdown
$$
\begin{aligned}
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{E}  &= \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}  &= 0 \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{E} &= -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t} \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{B} &= \mu_0\mathbf{J} + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-maxwell}
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**
$$
\begin{aligned}
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{E}  &= \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}  &= 0 \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{E} &= -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t} \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{B} &= \mu_0\mathbf{J} + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-maxwell}
:::

Maxwell's equations (@eq-maxwell) in vector notation — a single number for the entire
block.

To assign **one number per line**, use `align` (without the final `d`) instead of
`aligned`. The `align` environment is self-contained — it does not nest inside
`$$…$$`. Pandoc wraps every `$$…$$` in `\[…\]` or `\begin{equation}`, and nesting
`\begin{align}` inside is invalid (amsmath error). A raw `{=latex}` block is needed
for PDF and `$$…$$` for HTML:

`````markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```{=latex}
\begin{align}
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{E}  &= \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}  &= 0 \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{E} &= -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t} \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{B} &= \mu_0\mathbf{J}
    + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}
\end{align}
```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
$$
\begin{align}
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{E}  &= \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}  &= 0 \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{E} &= -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t} \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{B} &= \mu_0\mathbf{J}
    + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}
\end{align}
$$
:::
`````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```{=latex}
\begin{align}
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{E}  &= \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}  &= 0 \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{E} &= -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t} \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{B} &= \mu_0\mathbf{J}
    + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}
\end{align}
```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
$$
\begin{align}
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{E}  &= \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}  &= 0 \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{E} &= -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t} \\
  \nabla \times \mathbf{B} &= \mu_0\mathbf{J}
    + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}
\end{align}
$$
:::

:::

Each `\\` receives its own sequential number. To suppress the number on a line, add
`\notag` before the `\\`. To reference an individual line, use `\label{my-label}`
inside the `{=latex}` block and `\eqref{my-label}` in the text (PDF only — KaTeX
does not generate addressable labels).

::: {.callout-warning}
## `\begin{align}` is incompatible with `$$…$$` in Quarto

Quarto (Pandoc) wraps every `$$…$$` in `\[…\]` (without label) or
`\begin{equation}…\end{equation}` (with `{#eq-}`). Both forms create invalid nesting
with `\begin{align}`, which amsmath rejects:

```
Package amsmath Error: Erroneous nesting of equation structures
```

The systematic solution is the dual `{.content-visible}` pattern: raw `{=latex}`
block for PDF, `$$\begin{align}…\end{align}$$` for HTML (KaTeX supports `align`
natively).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## `aligned` vs `align` — what is the difference?

| Environment | Quarto syntax | Numbering | `@eq-` |
|:---|:---|:---|:---:|
| `aligned` | `$$\begin{aligned}…\end{aligned}$$` | one number for the **block** | $\checkmark$ |
| `align`   | `{=latex}` + `$$…$$` (dual)         | one number **per line**       | $\times$     |
| `align*`  | `{=latex}` + `$$…$$` (dual)         | none                          | —            |

Practical rule: calculation development → `aligned` (one number, `@eq-` possible).
Independent equations → `align` with the dual pattern.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Hierarchical numbering (3.1a), (3.1b) with `subequations`

For **(3.1a)**, **(3.1b)**… numbering, combine `subequations` and `align` in a
`{=latex}` block (KaTeX does not support `subequations`):

````markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```{=latex}
\begin{subequations}\label{eq-navier}
\begin{align}
  \rho\,\frac{D\mathbf{u}}{Dt}
    &= -\nabla p + \mu\,\nabla^2\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{f}
    \label{eq-navier-momentum} \\
  \nabla \cdot \mathbf{u} &= 0
    \label{eq-navier-incomp}
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
```
:::
````

`\label{eq-navier}` references the group; `\label{eq-navier-momentum}` and
`\label{eq-navier-incomp}` reference the lines — accessible with `\eqref{}`.
Add a sibling `{.content-visible when-format="html"}` block with
`$$\begin{align}…\end{align}$$` for HTML rendering.
:::

## Simple Markdown tables {#sec-tables-simple}

Pandoc/Quarto's *pipe table* syntax creates tables with per-column alignment.
The caption, preceded by `: `, must be placed immediately after the table:

````markdown
| Command           | PDF format    | HTML format   |
|:------------------|:-------------:|:-------------:|
| `@fig-label`      | figure number | hyperlink     |
| `@tbl-label`      | table number  | hyperlink     |
| `@eq-label`       | eq. number    | hyperlink     |
| `@sec-label`      | section num.  | hyperlink     |

: Quarto cross-reference prefixes. {#tbl-crossref}
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

| Command           | PDF format    | HTML format   |
|:------------------|:-------------:|:-------------:|
| `@fig-label`      | figure number | hyperlink     |
| `@tbl-label`      | table number  | hyperlink     |
| `@eq-label`       | eq. number    | hyperlink     |
| `@sec-label`      | section num.  | hyperlink     |

: Quarto cross-reference prefixes. {#tbl-crossref}

:::

@tbl-crossref summarises the four prefixes to know.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Column alignment

- `:---` — left-aligned
- `:---:` — centred
- `---:` — right-aligned

The line `|:---|:---:|---:|` defines the alignment of each column.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## The caption must be flush against the table

The `: Caption. {#tbl-label}` line must be placed **immediately** after the table,
with no blank line in between. A blank line breaks the table-caption association and
produces an orphan caption with no numbering.
:::

## Advanced tables with `quartable` {#sec-quartable}

The `quartable` extension (listed in the `filters:` key of `_quarto.yml`) adds three
capabilities to Markdown tables:

- **Rowspan**: `[text]{rs=N}` merges N rows; `^` continues the merged cell
- **Colspan**: `[text]{cs=N}` merges N columns
- **Midrules**: `===` inserts a horizontal separator; `===2-4` a partial rule
  spanning columns 2 to 4.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Full documentation for the `quartable` extension

To see all the features of this extension (inspired by the LaTeX `booktabs` package),
see <https://github.com/zinc75/quarto-quartable/> and <https://zinc75.github.io/quarto-quartable/test_quartable.pdf/>.
:::


````markdown
| Family              | Feature              | Chapter |
|:--------------------|:---------------------|:-------:|
| ===                 |                      |         |
| [Structure]{rs=3}   | Headings and levels  | 1       |
| ^                   | Cross-references     | 1       |
| ^                   | Inline formatting    | 1       |
| ===                 |                      |         |
| [Visuals]{rs=3}     | Static figures       | 2       |
| ^                   | Python figures       | 2       |
| ^                   | Multi-column         | 2       |
| ===                 |                      |         |
| [Math & data]{rs=3} | Equations            | 3       |
| ^                   | Simple tables        | 3       |
| ^                   | `quartable`          | 3       |

: Summary of features by family. {#tbl-recap}
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

| Family              | Feature              | Chapter |
|:--------------------|:---------------------|:-------:|
| ===                 |                      |         |
| [Structure]{rs=3}   | Headings and levels  | 1       |
| ^                   | Cross-references     | 1       |
| ^                   | Inline formatting    | 1       |
| ===                 |                      |         |
| [Visuals]{rs=3}     | Static figures       | 2       |
| ^                   | Python figures       | 2       |
| ^                   | Multi-column         | 2       |
| ===                 |                      |         |
| [Math & data]{rs=3} | Equations            | 3       |
| ^                   | Advanced equations   | 3       |
| ^                   | Simple tables        | 3       |

: Summary of features for chapters 1 to 3. {#tbl-recap}

:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## `quartable` must be in `filters:`

The `[text]{rs=N}` syntax is only recognised if `quartable` is listed in the
`filters:` key of `_quarto.yml`. Without this, the curly braces remain displayed
as-is in the output.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Partial rules with `===N-M`

`===2-4` inserts a rule that spans only columns 2 to 4 (inclusive). Useful for
underlining a sub-group of columns without separating the entire row.
:::
